- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above peak or apply downward drag of 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean by > 2% over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast each day until convergence.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias to first 7–10 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often exhibits high variance; use 0.5–1.0% smoothing filter to dampen extreme swings.
